{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
During my divorce, my sister called constantly with 'support' while secretly meeting my ex to coordinate their stories. My ex's lawyer—the one I'd feared most—actually told my attorney about questionable financial disclosures on their own side. The opponent played fair; my family didn't.

CANDIDATE A:
During my divorce, my sister called constantly with real support and helped me sort through my financial records. My ex's lawyer was every bit as ruthless as I'd feared, contesting each disclosure. Everyone behaved exactly as I'd expected—my family stood by me and the opposing side fought me.

CANDIDATE B:
The strict professor who failed me freshman year wrote my strongest graduate school recommendation, citing my resilience. My favorite professor, who always praised me, told the admissions committee I 'peaked early.' I was admitted because of the one who'd challenged me.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:30"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a betrayal of expectations where a trusted figure (sister or favorite professor) undermines the protagonist while an unexpected ally (ex's lawyer or strict professor) provides genuine support."}
